clue.text: Essential ingredient upsetting the apple-cart — Darn!

indicators.note: upsetting a cart tips its load out in disorder, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone spoils a carefully laid plan and swears about the vital element that was lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' rearranges the thirteen letters of APPLECART and DARN; the hyphen and the exclamation are only surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is part and parcel of a thing is an integral, inseparable component of it.

clue.text: Licence for every letter to 6

parts.note: per means for each, as in 'per head'
a missive is a letter or written message
6 down is CAPE, a headland; Ness is a word for a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Orford Ness

explanation.surface: A rule granting permission for each letter sent to a numbered address.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference '6' points to the answer at 6 down, a cape, whose synonym NESS (a promontory, as in Dungeness) ends the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Licence in the sense of excessive freedom or laxity is the quality of being overly tolerant.

clue.text: Bones, of king over 1974 years ago

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for rex, Latin for king
written in 1976, the clue points back to the year AD 2, written AD II in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A grim archaeological note about a king's bones dated nearly two millennia back.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle dates from 1976, so 1974 years earlier is AD II; with R (king) on top it gives the plural of a forearm bone.
explanation.definitionFit: The radius is a forearm bone, and its plural names more than one such bone.

clue.text: In advancing age, bishop follows' girl with short skirt

indicators.note: follows places the bishop's name straight after the girl's name

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
Odo of Bayeux was the bishop and half-brother of William the Conqueror
a mini is a short skirt

explanation.surface: An ageing churchman trails after a young woman in a miniskirt.
explanation.walkthrough: Odo of Bayeux, half-brother of William the Conqueror, is the bishop. The stray apostrophe after 'follows' is a printing blemish, and 'In' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquially the Latin year-of-our-Lord phrase is a jocular term for getting old, the years catching up with someone.

clue.text: Row about split in cinema

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: a din is a row, a loud noise
to rive is to split or tear apart

explanation.surface: An argument breaks out over a rift at the picture house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' reads as a line of seats in the cinema, but it is a noisy row, DIN, wrapped 'about' RIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A drive-in is an open-air cinema where the audience watches from parked cars.

clue.text: Pardon me! An awful pen!

indicators.note: awful suggests these short words are badly mangled into a new order

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs

explanation.surface: Someone apologises for a dreadful fountain pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pardon me!' looks like a whole apology, but only 'Pardon' defines; 'awful' turns ME AN into AMNE.
explanation.definitionFit: An amnesty is an official pardon granted to a group of offenders.

clue.text: Headgear

parts.note: read as two words: something that is a head (a promontory) and also gear (a garment you wear)

explanation.definitionFit: A cape is both a headland jutting into the sea and a sleeveless cloak, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Fall in love and get depressed

definitions.meaning: falling in love is surrendering one's affections to someone

explanation.surface: Romance leads straight to gloom.
explanation.definitionFit: To give one's heart to someone is to fall for them, while losing courage or hope is becoming dispirited.

clue.text: Some benefit changing about 0.1 krone prematurely

indicators.note: about means going around, so the rearranged letters surround the coin
changing signals that the letters of these two words are altered into a new arrangement

parts.note: the øre is a small Scandinavian coin worth a fraction of a krone (strictly one hundredth)

explanation.surface: A small part of a welfare payment is altered by a fraction of a Danish crown, and too soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' makes BEFONESTIME from the first two words, and 'about' wraps it round the coin. 'Some' looks like a selection signal but is fodder; an øre is really a hundredth of a krone.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done before one's time happens too early, ahead of the expected moment.

clue.text: Brave but embarrassed Hindu

parts.note: embarrassment makes one go red in the face
a Hindu is typically an Indian

explanation.surface: A courageous person is nonetheless flustered, a Hindu blushing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave' looks like an adjective but is the noun for a Native American warrior, the old (now offensive) term this answer gives.
explanation.definitionFit: A brave was a warrior of a North American tribe, for which this dated term was once common.

clue.text: Company leave drink unfinished

indicators.note: leave tells the solver to leave off part of the drink's name

parts.note: a posset is a hot drink of milk curdled with ale or wine
unfinished names the finishing letter of the drink as the part to be left off

explanation.surface: Soldiers on leave abandon their drinks half-drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: The drink is POSSET, a hot milk-and-ale drink; 'leave' it 'unfinished' means drop its finishing letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A posse is a band of people, especially one summoned by a sheriff, so a group or troop.

clue.text: Rejected by Parliament — one Greek work

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the Dáil is the lower house of the Irish parliament

explanation.surface: A bill is turned down by the legislators, one Greek's work among them.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dáil is Ireland's lower house of parliament; 'Rejected' makes it LIAD, after the numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic of the siege of Troy is a classic poem of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Letters to listen to in comfort

indicators.note: to listen to signals that the letters are heard rather than seen

parts.note: the plural of the letter E, written out as ees

explanation.surface: Correspondence to hear read aloud while relaxing in an armchair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters' is not correspondence but two of the letter E, spoken as a plural, which sounds like a word for comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: Ease is a state of relaxed comfort, freedom from pain or strain.

clue.text: Drive away in quiet circles

parts.note: sh is the call for silence
O is circle-shaped, so two circles give OO

explanation.surface: Someone motors off silently in loops.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoo is to scare off or send away, as with chickens.

clue.text: Fasten to bed — doctor's work if the task is unfinished

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
op is short for opus, a work
an is an archaic word for if

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter of the chore is lopped off

parts.note: a chore is a task

explanation.surface: A medic's job sounds incomplete, like tucking a patient up in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' looks like a hospital bed but is the sea bed. AN is archaic for 'if', as in Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: Dropping anchor secures a ship by lowering its hook to grip the bottom of the sea.

clue.text: Camper in Australia was, oddly, an American agent

indicators.note: oddly means in an odd way, so the short word is rearranged

parts.note: a G-man is an FBI agent in US slang

explanation.surface: A man camping in the outback was strangely a US federal agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' looks like taking odd letters but here rearranges WAS to SWA; the Australian swagman is an itinerant who carries his bundle, his swag.
explanation.definitionFit: A swagman was an Australian itinerant worker who tramped the country carrying his belongings, sleeping rough.

clue.text: A grain store erected in citadel

parts.note: a crop is a harvest of grain

indicators.note: erected means set upright, so in a down answer the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a silo is a tower for storing grain

explanation.surface: A tower for keeping corn has been built inside a fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'erected' turns the store upwards, reading OLIS. 'grain store' looks like one silo, but 'grain' gives its own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The Acropolis of Athens is the classic example of a hilltop citadel or fortified upper town.

clue.text: The total length from back to front of, for instance, a wagon

indicators.note: from back to front means the whole run of letters is read in reverse

parts.note: eg abbreviates exempli gratia, for example
a dray is a low heavy cart or wagon

explanation.surface: Measuring a wagon from its rear end to its front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from back to front' turns the whole run around, giving YARDAGE; a dray is a brewer's cart.
explanation.definitionFit: Yardage is a measurement expressed in yards, the total distance or extent of something.

clue.text: Queen in museum gallery

indicators.note: in places the monarch's letters within the museum's letters

parts.note: the V and A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: The monarch visits an exhibition hall.
explanation.walkthrough: The museum is the V&A, the Victoria and Albert Museum in London; 'gallery' means an open porch, not an art space.
explanation.definitionFit: A veranda is a roofed open platform along a house, a kind of porch or open-sided gallery.

clue.text: Attire's fancy for entertainer

indicators.note: fancy as a verb means imagine, and fanciful arrangement reshuffles these letters

parts.note: the word attire with its s, all used as letters

explanation.surface: Clothing that is elaborate befits a showman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges the seven letters ATTIRES, the apostrophe ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: An artiste is a professional performer, such as a singer or dancer.

clue.text: Turner for nautical work excels with colour

parts.note: to cap is to outdo or surpass
tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: A painter of seascapes outshines rivals in his use of colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' suggests the painter J. M. W. Turner and his seascapes, but it is a thing that turns.
explanation.definitionFit: A capstan is a revolving drum on a ship, used to wind in cables.

clue.text: Direction-finder — pity there's a bit missing

indicators.note: missing means a portion is absent from the longer word

parts.note: compassion is pity
an ion is a tiny particle, a bit of matter

explanation.surface: Regret that a navigation tool has lost a part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit' is not vague: it is ION, a tiny charged particle, removed from COMPASSION.
explanation.definitionFit: A compass shows magnetic north and so helps a traveller find their bearings.

clue.text: A bit of banana peel, that's scruffy!

definitions.note: the scruff is the back of the neck, so this is a playful way of saying it is the scruff

indicators.note: a bit of means only a small part of the words is taken

explanation.surface: Someone sees a scrap of banana skin and finds it untidy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scruffy' suggests untidiness, but it is playful: the part of the neck that is the scruff.
explanation.definitionFit: The back of the neck is also called the scruff, as when a cat is lifted by it.

clue.text: Staunch supporter

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to staunch is to check a flow
a stalk bearing a flower or leaf

explanation.definitionFit: To stem a flow is to stop it, as with blood; a stalk holds up a leaf or flower.

clue.text: Money in marks

definitions.meaning: paper currency in the form of banknotes
written jottings, or marks made as reminders

explanation.definitionFit: Banknotes are paper currency, and jottings are written marks.

clue.text: A portion of ice-cream for everybody

definitions.meaning: half the name of the mixed-fruit ice cream
the Italian musical term meaning all players together

explanation.surface: A serving of dessert shared among the whole party.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutti forms half the name of tutti-frutti ice cream, and in music it is the direction for all performers together.

clue.text: Fashionable cape in Rome, this

parts.note: C is the map abbreviation for cape
hic is the Latin word for this

explanation.surface: A stylish cloak worn in the Eternal City.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cape' tempts as a garment but is the abbreviation C; the Romans' Latin for 'this' is HIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic means stylish and elegant.

clue.text: Slender lass and mum about to travel around

indicators.note: around places the mother's word on either side of the travel word

parts.note: mum as in 'keep mum' means silent, sh

indicators.note: about signals that the travel word is turned to face the other way

parts.note: to ply is to travel regularly back and forth

explanation.surface: A thin girl and her mother are setting off on a world tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' is not mother but the call for silence; 'about' gives YLP, which 'around' places inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sylph is a slim, graceful girl, after the airy spirits of folklore.

clue.text: GP ate this well-cooked food

indicators.note: well-cooked means thoroughly mixed up, as ingredients are, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The family doctor ate this thoroughly done dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well-cooked' rearranges GP ATE THIS; 'GP' looks like a doctor but is just two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti is pasta in long thin strands, a staple dish.

clue.text: Offices rejected by office agents

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: terce is one of the canonical hours, a church office said at the third hour
a church service is an office

explanation.surface: Departments turned down by the bureau's spies.
explanation.walkthrough: TERCE is a daily church office (the third hour); 'rejected' reverses TERCES, and SERVICE is another word for an office.
explanation.definitionFit: The secret service is a government intelligence organisation, made up of spies.
